The proposed answer, $c = 1/22$, matches what I recall of the Konyagin–Shkredov quantitative Beurling–Helson result, in which $\|e^{-2\pi i z\phi}\|_{A(\mathbb T)} = O(\log^{1/22-\varepsilon}|z|)$ forces $\phi$ to be affine. I can't check the paper here, so this rests on memory rather than verification. The exponent is the key point, and I have no independent evidence that a later result improved it.

The background paragraph has some loose claims. Kahane's conjecture and the $\sqrt{\log\log}$-type partial result are attributed from memory and aren't needed for the answer. The derivation of $c$ is only sketched and cites no specific lemma, so the boxed value rests on the citation.
